lines: Kirara
What is this... what a nectar...
That was her first reaction after tasting the ice cream from Inage's shop.
Kirara
So cold, so sweet... how luxurious... Ah, I shouldn't... I can't stop my hands...
Saying that, she kept eating, one bite after another.
After finishing it with such enthusiasm, Kirara finally let out a satisfied sigh.
Kirara
Hah... I have thoroughly enjoyed it... Ahh...
Only then did she seem to snap back to reality, her eyes widening.
She clearly remembered being so engrossed in the sweets, turning bright red as she bowed her head.
Kirara
I am deeply sorry, again and again... I must have looked so undignified...
Me
It's fine. Everyone here loves the ice cream, so I'm glad you enjoyed it.
Now that we had eaten something sweet and cold, it was time to balance it out with some bitter, warm tea.
Me
Please, it's just a simple tea.
Matcha culture began during the Sengoku period, but by the Edo era, even commoners were drinking simple sencha.
The scenes in period dramas where tea and dango are served at tea shops are probably quite famous.
It is said that tea processing techniques improved around the mid-Edo period, but setting that aside...
Kirara
Delicious... This must be quite expensive...
Me
It's cheap when served at a place like this.
A complaint from Natsu about us meddling in her business flew out, and Kirara chuckled.
Kirara
Lady Natsu has a demeanor similar to my grandmother.
Me
Nice, Grandma. They say you have the air of a leader.
A kiseru was thrown silently and hit me, then returned to Natsu's hand.
Me
(What kind of skill is that...)
Seeing me pat my head, Kirara continued to giggle.
Kirara
Abundant and peaceful... It is a peaceful world I could never have imagined in my time...
Compared to the Sengoku period, early Edo was peaceful, but a developing nation had few resources.
People are content, and there is no conflict. That is the peace she had envisioned, and perhaps the modern era is its realization.
Me
(Or perhaps she could see some specific conflict looming on the horizon.)
Even in a period when large-scale wars had subsided, in the world of ninjas, there would surely have been sparks of conflict, big or small.
I should not lightly intrude on whatever issues Kirara might be carrying.
Me
I see... that must be it, surely.
So I replied with what was on my mind, but I could not tell how she took it.
Kirara
So, in your daily life... how do you spend your time?
She took another sip of tea before asking that.
Me
How... well, first there is school.
Kirara
School... a place of learning for ninjas, I suppose.
Me
For us, yes. But even those who are not ninjas, most children attend school with the support of the state.
Of course, we also have regular classes.
Kirara
At the academy, do you study ninjutsu and swordsmanship?
Me
Yes, we have classes for training and cultivation. Besides that, the organization assigns missions suited to our abilities, so we carry those out.
Kirara
I see... Even if it looks peaceful, it is not entirely peaceful, is it...
Kirara murmured that softly, but then she seemed to snap out of it, lifting her face and fumbling for words to cover up her slip.
Kirara
I-I am so sorry, that was rude of me... I had no intention of criticizing you at all...
Me
It is fine. Besides, our work is to create peace... If you think of it that way, it actually gives us quite a bit of motivation.
Kirara
To create peace...
I had not thought it through deeply, but hearing the words that had come out of me in the moment, she seemed to be deeply moved.
Kirara
...I think that is a noble perspective.
It seemed she had sensed that I was not offended, for Kirara showed a look of relief.
Me
Besides, there's time outside of training and missions. If nothing's going on, I might stop by this shop with friends on the way home from school, or something like that.
Other than that, it's probably just the time I spend with Tokiko and the rest of the family after getting home.
Kirara
With your family... does that mean you perform any special training or rituals at home?
Me
It depends on the person, and it depends on the family.
If a family has a unique power that requires specific rituals or training to use, they would likely perform them.
I myself have asked the Library to arrange personal training sessions that I continue on my own.
There might be families that enforce such practices, but ultimately, it varies from case to case.
Me
Including all of that, it might just be our daily life.
Kirara
I see...
As if remembering something, she gazes into the distance and murmurs.
Kirara
I had my own daily life, too, between my regular training and... my work.
Kirara
But... even though it should be the same, everyone here seems somehow brighter... There's no look of despair on your faces.
That is perhaps something that cannot be helped.
The ninjas of that era were, so to speak, hardcore practitioners.
Killing and being killed were truly part of their daily existence. They must have lived with the constant awareness that it could happen to them at any moment.
However, voicing that now would be an indulgence born of living in a relatively peaceful era. It is not something I should be saying.
Me
Well, there are more of us now, and we specialize in different fields, so the burden on each individual is lighter.
I inferred the difference between the two eras and answered as such.
Still, I imagine that for ninjas of the past, everything from information gathering to planning and execution was a one-man operation.
If ordered from above to do something, they would think through everything necessary to carry it out and execute it, taking full personal responsibility as a matter of course.
Even in modern times, ultimate responsibility is personal, but much of the information can be obtained in advance. Sometimes, we are simply executing a strategy devised by our superiors.
It is not exactly a work-style reform, but the variety of entertainment available has also contributed to a relaxation in everyone's mindset.
I conveyed this to Kirara in terms she could understand, and after a moment, she gave a small nod.
Kirara
...I must have felt that there was a freedom in the truest sense of the word.
Me
Freedom, you say?
Kirara paused for a moment to think, then began to speak haltingly.
Kirara
The Hatagashire clan of Iga... had a long-standing grudge with the Man'yoku Valley of Koga...
The conflict between Iga and Koga had lasted for four hundred years.
It was only forcibly suppressed because of a non-aggression pact made with the current Hattori Hanzo and his predecessor.
However, the period during which they were forbidden from fighting had only been a few decades at most.
In that time, the resentment did not fade; rather, it seemed to simmer and intensify, making each side despise the other.
Kirara
Amidst all that, a turning point arrived... It was the visit of Koga's Man'yoku Valley, Lord Danjo's grandson... Lord Koga Gennosuke.
The grandson of the Koga head had come to meet the grandson of the Iga head—Kirara herself—along with the head himself.
Me
So, it was a matchmaking meeting?
Kirara
N-Yes... that's right...
Kirara, blushing red to the tips of her ears and looking shy, looked nothing like the heir to the ninja clan; she was simply a girl of her age.
Kirara
A-Anyway... Kirara and Lord Koga Gennosuke both disapproved of our clans fighting, and we were exploring a path toward reconciliation.
Me
So... you both took a liking to each other and got close enough to promise to marry?
Kirara
...Mm... Ah... Ugh... Yes...
That's a nice story.
But judging by her words, things hadn't gone smoothly.
I couldn't help but project the situation onto Nisha Gaiza or my own father.
Kirara
If... Kirara and Lord Koga Gennosuke had been born in a bright, peaceful era like this...
As she spoke, she seemed to have recalled the next head of the Koga clan, her intended.
She murmured that softly.
Kirara
Blessed by everyone... and being able to unite... I cannot help but think that...
I see—.
It seems she hopes that their marriage will bring the two clans closer together, but there were likely many who did not share that view.
After all, having long hated each other, they had just entered a state of no-war, and stress was beginning to build up. For such talk to come up at that moment—
The feeling of "why should we be with those people" must have been on the verge of exploding.
In a sense, the timing could be said to have been far too bad.
Kirara
...But... even so, I...
Me
Yes.
Kirara
...I do not intend to give up.
Is that because she loves him that much?
Or is it because she wants to end the days where lives are lost pointlessly by linking Iga and Koga?
Me
(It is surely both.)
Though immature as a shinobi, she will eventually stand above the other shinobi as head of the clan and have to send them on missions that could kill them.
Even if that is an unavoidable future, if she can reduce such missions and conflicts even a little, that would be the best outcome.
If the way to bring about that best outcome is for her to unite with the one she loves, there is no reason she must give up.
Her position as the future head of the clan, and her position as a girl who simply thinks of the one she loves—
She is trying to take every action she can think of, refusing to neglect either side.
Me
...I think that is truly admirable.
It is a way of thinking worthy of respect.
As the head of the clan, she possesses a strength that I must learn from.
Kirara
No... I am just being selfish...
Me
I think that is fine. From what I have seen, clan heads are surprisingly often that kind of person.
Whether it was my father or Nisha Gaiza, if you pushed it to the extreme, they seemed to hold a prominent, selfish desire where their own wishes came first.
Me
(If there is a problem... it is what happens when they think too hard about it.)
The two who came to mind were no exception—.
If that energy is directed outward, it explodes; if it is held in too long, it leads to ruin.
Kirara seems to be the kind who leans toward the path of ruin.
Is there anything I can do for someone like her?
Me
(Well, I doubt there is much I can do, but still...)
Lost in thought, I suddenly stand up.
Kirara
Fuuma-sama...?
Me
Let us stretch our legs for a while.
As I say this, I raise both hands overhead and stretch my body out.
Me
Thinking is necessary. But if it becomes a dead end, we need to loosen up our minds to change our perspective.
Kirara
H-Huh...
Me
For now... how about we act our age, at least while we are away from our relatives?
In another era, Kirara would still be a student.
Going to school, taking detours on the way home, playing with friends, spending time with family...
Perhaps she needs that kind of time.
With that in mind, I make my suggestion, and she falls silent for a moment.
Kirara
...Fuuma-sama, what do your friends usually call you?
Me
Eh... right... Just your name, or Fuuma-kun, I suppose...
I briefly explain that "-kun" is a common honorific used for men.
Kirara
...Then, Fuuma-kun, shall I say?
Me
Hm?
I reply with a confused tone, and she lets out a small, suppressed laugh.
Kirara
Since you said to act our age... could you please continue guiding us, Fuuma-kun?
Saying that, she stands up as well.
I may have inadvertently made things awkward for her.
Thinking that, I nod.
Me
Understoo—no, got it. Then let's go, Kirara.
Kirara
Yes. Thank you.
I hope that her smile brings even a slight sense of peace to my heart.
I could not help but wish for that.
